name: Coma Berenices
introduction: is Berenice’s Hair. According to legend, Queen Berenice II of Egypt offered her hair to the gods for her husband’s safe return from war; when it disappeared from the temple, the court astronomer declared that it had been placed among the stars. It is a faint but beautiful region best seen on northern spring evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Looking toward Coma Berenices, we look straight out of the disk of the Milky Way: the north galactic pole lies here. With little dust in the way, deep space opens up.

The Coma Cluster, about 320 million light-years away, contains more than a thousand galaxies. In 1933, Fritz Zwicky found that they move too fast to be held together by their visible matter, one of the first clues to dark matter.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Beta Comae Berenices](hip:64394), 30 light-years away, is a star very similar to the Sun. [Diadem](hip:64241) is a binary whose two stars orbit almost edge-on to us every 26 years. [Gamma Comae Berenices](hip:60742) is an orange giant at the edge of the Coma Star Cluster.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The Coma Star Cluster, a loose spray of faint stars about 280 light-years away, gives the constellation its look of flowing hair. Galaxies here include the Black Eye Galaxy, M64, with its dark band of dust, and the Needle Galaxy, NGC 4565, seen exactly edge-on. The northern part of the Virgo Cluster also extends into Coma Berenices.
